notes.title: ‘Dungeons 4 – Tales from the Campfire’ DLC releases June 26th!
notes.content:
[h1]‘Dungeons 4 – Tales from the Campfire’ DLC releases June 26th![/h1]

The Ultimate Evil is thrilled to announce the third DLC for [b]Dungeons 4, titled ‘Tales from the Campfire’ launching June 26th[/b] on Steam, Xbox PC, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation®5 and Nintendo Switch™.

Dungeons 4 – Tales from the Campfire introduces a [b]brand-new four-mission campaign[/b] featuring the Narrator, the mischievous Gorgu (a.k.a the Baby Evil), the Absolute Evil’s right-hand elf Thalya, and her sickeningly virtuous stepbrother Tristan. The DLC will also grant players even [b]more evil customisation for Thalya as she receives four new skills[/b].
Just when Thalya and Tristan thought they had escaped to their home dimension following the events of ‘Not Another Multiverse’, fate had other plans! Instead of safely returning to Thalya’s beloved dungeon and Tristan’s pretentiously perfect fortress, they’re thrown off course and forced to journey back the hard way. Along the way Gorgu throws tantrum after tantrum, threatening the safety of their camp (and the sanity of both siblings). 
Join this less-than-merry group as they set up camp for the night and attempt to lull the Diaper-Wearing Evil to a restful slumber with four devious tales from the past (which are, of course, the most calming bedtime stories for a future Dungeon Lord ). These include: [b]a mission to  recapture Gorgu’s toy and destroy the heroes’ stronghold,, a dastardly plot to blow up a mail train (in case you were wondering – yes, this is why your package is delayed), a dramatic fight in the depths of a fiery volcano, and a climactic battle against the Knight of the Order of the Sheep[/b]. Set up camp, grab your marshmallows, and prepare to play through for a collection of evil bedtime stories like no other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/cea36b79379a15e7b807dac2f7a123ed282db32e.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/a8a29fe94e0ccc3a04389c4b1aa2ee803b1f0e1f.jpg[/img]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3707110/Dungeons_4__Tales_from_the_Campfire/
[b]Dungeons 4 – Tales from the Campfire will release on June 26th on Steam, Xbox PC, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch.[/b]

[h3]Features:[/h3]
[list]
[*] “Tales from the Campfire” enriches the world of Dungeons 4 with four bone-chilling, fully voiced campaign missions; each telling a story fit to calm the unruly (and incredibly loud) soul of the Regrowing Evil.
[*] Mission 1 “Gorgu’s Toy” starts out with the meanest theft in history – those pesky heroes have stolen Gorgu’s favourite toy mirror. Act fast to regain this treasured item before Gorgu’s tears flood your dungeon and drown your wildest dreams of evil supremacy.
[*] Mission 2 is called “The Great Mail Robbery”. You might be sensing a recurring theme here, but this time, you are on the right side of the story: Catapulted back to the Wicked Wild West you’re aim is to rob a mail train! Sounds like a lot of fun, doesn’t it?
[*] Mission 3 “Molten Core” is not for the weak willed, Thalya’s icy heart won’t be enough, you’ll need all the help you can get to cool down a steaming-hot, highly explosive volcano – even if it means working together with Tristan and his heroes.
[*] In Mission 4 we reach our fluffy finale with “Counting Sheep, Dungeon Style”: In the idyllic realm of the Knights of the Order of the Sheep, heroes wield a different kind of magic, turning your gruesome servants of Evil into fluffy, nerve-rackingly bleating sheep. But perhaps the Explosion-Loving Evil can use some sheep of its own...?
[*] Throughout all these stories, four new skills for Thalya will make sure your sweetest dreams come true – “Bad Air”, “Indomitable Horde”, “Hero Graves”, “Dark Side”.
[/list]

notes.title: Kalypso Media Expands Portfolio into Educational Apps
notes.content:
[h1]Kalypso Media Expands Portfolio into Educational Apps [/h1]

[h2]Gabble is set to Release on May 20th [/h2]

[b]Bracknell, UK – March 30, 2025[/b] – Kalypso Media and the Ultimate Multilingo Evil are thrilled to announce their expansion into the world of education. [u]The Beginning[/u] is a groundbreaking project we have been developing for years in collaboration with some of the most talented and renowned linguistic researchers. 

[b]Gabble is a brand-new translator app[/b] that supports the [b]translation of Gobble[/b] into 42 languages. Become closer than ever with your feathered neighbours, understand what they are yelling at you when you are chasing them and learn more about their deep appreciation for corn – all made possible with Gabble! 
  
[b]Project Lead Thalya[/b] highlighted the vision behind the initiative: 
[i] "We wanted to create something with a real impact—something that would improve everybody's lives and bring all of us closer together. In our increasingly globalized world, the ability to connect and communicate across cultures has never been more important." [/i]

[b]According to the Divided Dungeon Dictators,[/b] [b]Gobblers[/b] now make up the largest population worldwide], [b]making Gobble the most spoken language on the planet[/b]. Yet, efforts to integrate them into society have been severely lacking—until now. 
  
Following extensive negotiations and productive collaborations, [b]Dr. Execu Tioner, CEO of Kenytucky Fried Gobbler (KFG)[/b], shared his excitement: 

[i]"At Kenytucky Fried Gobbler, we greatly appreciate this opportunity to work closely with Kalypso Media to be able to provide users with genuine value for their lives. We've already begun renovations to establish dedicated areas where customers can engage in conversation with Gobblers while waiting for their meals. 
 In the past, this was not possible due to... well, a number of unfortunate incidents and related safety concerns. Let’s just say our customers didn’t always make it out unscathed. But thanks to Kalypso Media’s new app, this is the biggest game-changer for us since the invention of buckets and deep fryers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/26a0a3f7533f3e227279f285351bd2aa29c684f8.jpg[/img]

Of course, we have spared no expense or effort to ensure that there are always enough Gobblers available for every test." [/i]

An excited KFG customer told us: [i]“Being able to talk to the Gobblers before consumption makes the meals feel so much more personalized. It would be truly heartwarming to get to know their backstory – It would definitely allow me to connect more." [/i]

[b]The Ultimate Multilingo Evil, Head of PR-Disasters[/b], spits out some final words – definitely not to convince everyone to use the App and start a new cult: 

[i]“Before we smash the gobblers into the best meal in the world, we make sure they feel loved and have room to speak their last wishes. With Gabble, we can now understand them!  

We sincerely hope you enjoy learning this language with our evil- uhm, efficient translator app. What do you mean, you haven’t used the app today? Daily usage is absolutely necessary *clenches fists in rage*!” [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/37fa78b7e2675489694d3f70867dfd4744dce726.jpg[/img]

[b]Gabble will be available May 20th[/b] on all mobile devices and smartwatches, with [b]physical editions[/b] of learning materials launching in select stores [b]on May 29th.[/b] 

[b]Kalypso Media Producer Evilge Nius[/b] hints that Gabble is just the beginning: 
[i] "This is only our first step into educational technology. Our developers are working hard on loot boxes with exclusive skins for the translation app. In fact, our first Succubi App Skin—available as a mythic drop in loot boxes—is nearly complete. 
 Later in 2025, we will introduce the Tropican Llama Translator, further cementing our commitment to educational apps and ensuring that every unheard voice is finally recognized. 
 We have plenty more content in the works—so stay tuned!"[/i] 

[b]Gabble will be free to download[/b] on all mobile devices and smartwatches. Retail edition dictionaries will be available in selected regions on May 29th. 

Players who pre-register will unlock an [b]exclusive Thalya ASMR translator voice[/b] for Gabble. 

[b]Gabble will release on May 20th (year unknown) for all your common devices. [/b]

[h3]Gabble Features: [/h3]
[list][*] [b]More fun than slaying heroes:[/b] By using this translator app, you learn a new language - the Gobblers' language! 
[*] [b]Translation into 42 languages: [/b]Gabble can translate the language of the Gobblers into 42 languages! A list of all languages can be found in the app by going through several unnecessary menu steps. 
[*] [b]Ready for use, 24/7:[/b] Whenever you're in the mood for some gobbler food- uhm, some gobbler interaction, Gabble is your tool for communication! The only requirement is a smartphone or a smart watch (not included with the app). Don’t you have phones? 
[*] [b]Gabble, Gobble or Goobble:[/b] The app can automatically understand the gobblers with the integrated audio detection. Just turn on the microphone and the app will do its part. (Access to the microphone, your camera and all your private data is extremely necessary.) [/list]

[h3]### [/h3]

For more information, please contact the Dungeons [b]Permanently-Redacted (PR)-Team[/b]

notes.title: Showcase and Contest Winner
notes.content:
[h1]Dungeons 4 – Contest Showcase and Winner Announcement[/h1]

[i]Faithful Underlings,[/i]

Following the announcement of the Badges of Honor, the Ultimate Evil now unveils a closer look at the masterfully crafted maps submitted for the contest.

[u][h2]Dungeons of the Apex[/h2][/u]

[b]Created by:[/b] Ice-Design
[b]Map Type:[/b] MOBA
[b]Overview:[/b] In this MOBA-like map, your objective is to destroy the enemy dwarf's main base.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/4a8e257afa341db8192d810a86287becf1cd5608.jpg[/img]

[b]Gameplay and Summary[/b]
You start in your dungeon and must build an army. The map features three lanes, each containing multiple buildings for both teams. Victory requires destroying all enemy bases in each lane before advancing to demolish the main base. Simultaneously, you must defend your dungeon heart and your team's bases. Minion waves spawn on each lane, progressing towards the enemy base and targeting enemy turrets. These waves grow stronger over time. Destroying certain overworld buildings also alters the dungeon's structure.

[b]What We Enjoyed[/b]
This lengthy map introduces a unique playstyle, requiring strategic thinking as you can't control your units once they're in a lane. This creates a distinct experience compared to typical Dungeons maps, making it a refreshing challenge.

[u][h2]Thalya and the 7 Dwarves[/h2][/u]

[b]Created by:[/b] wildmick
[b]Map Type:[/b] Kill Quest
[b]Overview:[/b] Begin in a uniquely structured dungeon and battle dwarves to achieve the required kills.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/c5a26b7985b1bcc9f6cfa63e9a674a6321647620.jpg[/img]

[b]Gameplay and Summary[/b]
This extensive map tasks you with building an army to kill as many dwarves as possible.

[b]What We Enjoyed[/b]
The symmetrical and unique map structure makes dungeon-building highly satisfying, providing a fresh take on the traditional gameplay.

[u][h2]Little Story of Snow White[/h2][/u]

[b]Created by:[/b] Legomaniak
[b]Map Type:[/b] Short-Story
[b]Overview:[/b] Thalya and seven dwarves must triumph over the queen.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/43f4dcab5841a46ab82c21cd5247efcffe3aac6a.png[/img]

[b]Gameplay and Summary[/b]
After a brief intro, you start with Thalya and must dig out seven dwarves with the help of snots. Use the units at your disposal to defeat the evil queen.

[b]What We Enjoyed[/b]
This short map features a clear objective and a fixed number of units, encouraging strategic thinking and unit preservation.

[u][h2]A Dwarf is seldom alone[/h2][/u]

[b]Created by:[/b] Test 9000
[b]Map Type:[/b] Small Skirmish Map
[b]Overview:[/b] Your objective is to destroy the 4 dwaven bases on the overworld. In addition 3 further bases have settled in the underground.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/f24dd5ceae83b205f72dbcf21a748a441771d228.png[/img]
 
[b]Gameplay and Summary[/b]
Dwarves are peculiar, you rarely meet a single one, often they come in droves and search for gold, stirring up the whole underground while doing so. Of course, the Absolute Evil doesn't like this at all.
The map is smaller but packed with details on the overworld, all in the magic blue glowing mushroom theme. Heroes and the dwarves in the underground will periodically attack your Dungeonheart. Use the predefinded way to place traps. Expansion is also more tricky since the space that can be excavated is defined though clear granite borders.

[b]What we enjoyed[/b]
A dwarf and mushroom focussed map with a love to detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/8c71fdeb416c85ba33f5ea06f0051fd3a8a75fff.png[/img]

[h2]Contest Winner[/h2]

After a long and painstaking deliberation process, the Ultimate Evil is pleased to announce the contest winner and Badge of Honor recipients. Each of the four maps are an "malevolent masterpiece," and thus, all four creators will receive the Badge of Honor. However, only one can be crowned the ultimate winner. After much consideration, the winner is <Ice-Design with Dungeons of the Apex>, who will be awarded the special version of the Badge. The technical realisation was a masterpiece and also caused amazement internally.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/59aa3bdb95726e8314591552ab0ca74964b577a3.jpg[/img]

This workshop and contest was new and exciting for us, and we had a lot of fun. We eagerly look forward to what the future holds, thanks to the awesomely evil Dungeons 4 community.

Thank you!
And remember:
[u][b]Stay Evil![/b][/u]

[h3]Dungeons 4 Editor leaves Beta today with Update 1.5, allowing console players to enjoy community-created maps for the first time[/h3]

With Update 1.5. Creators on PC can use the editor to [b]create content for players on PC, Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation 5[/b] to download and play!

From today, those who wish to unearth these player-generated-gems need only venture to the Mod.io section from the main menu, select from the vast array of maps, and prepare to destroy their foes in new and exciting ways.

[previewyoutube=TTr45HjOStc;full][/previewyoutube]

The editor allows aspiring developers of evil access to the same tools used by Realmforge Studios when building levels, including creating unique objectives, unique spawn conditions for units, and even adding custom dialogue. The only limit to the possibilities is how diabolical you are willing to be in pursuit of true evil!


[h1]Dungeons 4 - Update 1.5 [/h1]

[h2]Changes Update 1.5:[/h2]
[h3] Mod.io (Download Mods)[/h3]
[list]
[*] Mod.io access has been added to consoles. Players can now subscribe to and manage their mods via this new interface. [/list]

[h3]Level Editor[/h3]
[list][*] The Level Editor has now been fully released. After implementation of community feedback, polishing, and improvements, the Editor is no longer in its Beta phase.
[*] Additional fixes and features have been included in the Editor. Additional feature requests through the community and modding workshop have also been included.[/list]

[h3]Possess Snots![/h3]
[list][*] The new spell “Possess Little Snot” has been added to the game. This spell allows you to slip from your godlike position into the dungeon's simplest creature: A little Snot. “Work! Work! Wait, do I have to do all this myself now?”
[/list]

[h3]UI/UX[/h3]
[list]
[*] The main menu has been reworked. "Community Content" has been added to the main menu. When selecting "Community Maps", the downloaded maps can be played here (access to the downloaded maps is also possible via the "Skirmish" menu). When selecting "Find More Maps" the Mod.io interface opens. This is where all community content can be managed. 
[list][*] [PC only] When selecting "Editor", the player can edit or create new maps. [/list]
[*] The tile marker iconography has been improved to allow for better recognition of the iconography for colour vision impaired players.
[*] The size of unit names now changes correctly after adjusting the Font Size in the options menu.
[*] Single target spells now highlight their target correctly.
[*] The unit dungeon tooltip is now displayed correctly when you hover over a unit while it is standing in a dungeon room.
[*] Fixed an issue where mini-map icons of imprisoned enemies were being displayed incorrectly after loading a save game.
[*] Improved an error message when trying to build a work unit / gimmick outside of a room.
[/list]

[h3]Gamepad (Controller)[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved the tutorial of the introduction to the spell menu when using a game pad.
[*] The handling of ring-menus when using the game pad has been adjusted.
[*] The speed of scrolling within the level selection has been adjusted when using a gamepad.
[*] [PS5 Only] The speed of scrolling within the options menu has been adjusted when using a gamepad.
[*] The scrolling of the game hint menu has been improved when using a gamepad.
[/list]

[h3]Controls[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed input issues when using both a mouse and controller.
[*] Improved the behaviour when using CTRL+Click on a unit portrait in the unit selection.
[/list]

[h3]Other[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved the collider of portals to allow for better selection and easier transfer of units.
[*] The use of perk potions has been reworked. Perk potions are now unlocked immediately after researching the Voodoo Brew and can be produced immediately without any other requirements.
[*] Fixed an issue where Snots and some other units would go through visually closed doors.
[*] Fixed an issue where golden portals would not get marked as preferred targets after slapping them.
[*] Implemented several minor performance and memory optimisations.
[*] Fixed an issue where the selected Thalya skin would reset to default if the changes weren’t applied in the options menu.
[*] Fixed an issue where Thalya’s revive animation would display incorrectly after saving or loading a game.
[*] Fixed an issue where Thalya was unable to cast her spells while sitting on the throne.
[*] Fixed an issue where the dungeon lord was not re-summonable after dismissing him.
[*] Fixed an issue where the behaviour of the Hypno-Bullfrog was not working as intended after the first two attacks.
[*] Fixed an issue where some visual spell effects were not being displayed with the correct timing.
[*] Fixed an issue where some skills or traps were able to target units in the fog of war, which was unintended.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused unresponsive input behaviour when demolishing unpaid rooms.
[*] Improved a visual glitch which occurred when demolishing a torture work unit / gimmick.
[*] Improved some graphical glitches appearing on the Ice Tomb floor.
[*] Improved some visually flickering decals appearing during skirmish map “Dreamdungeon”.

[*] “Camera movement speed” and “Fast camera movement mode” added: These options allow you to adjust the camera movement to your liking. The fast camera movement mode can be used by default when holding shift while moving the camera with WASD when playing on keyboard and by holding LB while moving the camera when playing via gamepad. 
[*] “Potentially unpleasant sounds” option added to the options menu: This option can be used to mute potentially unpleasant noises such as the heartbeat of the dungeon heart or chewing noises (from creatures and other sources). 
[*] “Hand of Terror visible” added to the options menu: Switching off this option will hide the Hand of Terror in the dungeon whenever possible. 
[*] Fixed an issue where changing the key bindings would show incorrect conflicts between dungeon and overworld hotkeys. [/list]

[h3]User Interface & Controls [/h3]
[list][*] Improved behavior when giving multiple consecutive movement orders to your units in quick succession. Previously, units were prevented from moving quickly to the new movement point and appeared jittery.

[*] Improved the Hand of Terror appearing jittery to the other player when playing in co-op.  
[*] [Mouse & Keyboard] You can now return to the previous menus with a right mouse click. 
[*] [Gamepad] Adjusted the scroll speed in several menus. 
[*] [Gamepad] Units can now be renamed. [/list]

[h3]Gameplay & General Fixes [/h3]
[list][*] Added a level progression over time to Dwarven units in the dungeon (outside of the main campaign). 
[*] Fixed an issue where creeps and heroes would leave remains when they get relieved and are replaced by stronger groups. 
[*] Manavores now heal when eating mana (Better pay attention to them, or you will experience exponential growth in real time!). 
[*] Fixed an issue where Manavores were not restarting the search for new mana spots after their target mana spot was picked up and dropped by the player. 
[*] Added a distinct unconscious icon (“seeing stars” icon instead of just a skull icon) to unconscious heroes. 
[*] Potions now heal a fixed amount of health. 
[*] Added more information to the victory screen statistics. 
[*] Added a new mini-map icon to overworld hero spawners when they are destroyed. 
[*] Improved the general color scheme of enemy health and during enemy healing. 
[*] Improved the display of health bars in general and in relation to long object or unit names. 
[*] Improved the skill area display marker of enemy bosses and towers (especially for better visibility on snow). 
[*] The behavior of good creatures (mini-bosses) when fighting in their arenas has been improved. They now refrain from going too far out of their area and no longer receive invulnerability and healing too often when trying to return to the center of their arena. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Crystal Golem would teleport far outside his arena area. 
[*] Further fixes to Snots sometimes disappearing under mysterious circumstances (related to the collection of resources). 
[*] Fixed an issue where unconscious heroes would get dragged to unfinished torture devices that were still under construction. 
[*] Fixed an issue where dungeon enemies would not get visually caught by the Slime Ball trap. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Hamster Wheel of Death and Slime Ball trap placement would conflict with uncovered hidden rooms. 
[*] Fixed an issue where Thalya’s “The Heroes’ Grave” skill ability would trigger during some cinematic cutscenes and spawn ghost heroes when your creatures died in the cutscenes. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Dungeon Lord instantly appeared when moving him from the overworld to the dungeon. 
[*] Fixed an issue where canceling Thalya’s abilities would cost Evilness even though the casting of the ability was canceled. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Pit Fiend couldn’t be dropped on Dungeon exits. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Pit Fiend couldn’t be summoned after dismissing the unit previously. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Graveyard Tomb names were always displayed as “Banshee’s Tomb”. 
[*] Fixed an issue where some Dwarven units would sometimes bring excess Gold to the overworld and then get stuck there. 
[*] Fixed an issue where some Dwarven units were not visually opening Dwarven doors. 
[*] Fixed visual issues with Thalya which occurred while she was imprisoned in the cage. 
[*] Fixed an issue where Thalya’s passive skills were not being displayed correctly in the in-game menu (when pressing ESC while playing). [/list]

[h3]Animations & Visual Effects & Sounds [/h3]
[list][*] Added cheering animations to the creatures when the Dungeon Lord is summoned. 
[*] Added a walking animation to heroes when they are imprisoned. 
[*] Improved some animations when Thalya is wearing her Sailor Suit outfit. 
[*] Improved the visual effects related to picking up and holding some of the resources in the Hand of Terror. 
[*] Added occasional comments from Thalya when she kills an enemy, is revived, or gets a new level. 
[*] Added sounds when using toggle on/off buttons. 
[*] Fixed incorrect step sounds in the fog of war. 
[*] Improved the sounds of the Dungeon Lord.  
[*] Fixed an issue where Thalya’s and the Narrator’s greeting voice lines would overlap during startup.[/list]

[h3]Localization [/h3]
[list][*] Fixed a spelling mistake in the description of when horde units needed Beer to satisfy their needs. It now states correctly that horde units need Beer starting with level 6.

notes.title: OUT NOW! Dungeons 4 - Unleashes The Absolute Evil on the Overworld
notes.content:
[h1]OUT NOW! Dungeons 4 Unleashes The Absolute Evil on the Overworld[/h1]
[h1]Evil never looked so good [/h1]

Beware do-gooders of the Overworld, for war is on the horizon. [b]The Absolute Evil has officially been unleashed upon the Overworld[/b] with the official launch of Dungeons series’ highly anticipated sequel, Dungeons 4. 
Sound the alarm and prepare your traps, because Dungeons 4 is now available on [b]Steam, day one on Xbox Game Pass for console and PC Game Pass for PC[/b] and is available in Standard or Deluxe Editions on [b]Xbox Series X|S, Windows PC, and PlayStation 5[/b]. The [b]Deluxe Edition[/b] provides hellish extras for the most daring minions, including the [b]Digital Artbook[/b], [b]exclusive Dungeons 3 Evil Hand Legacy Skin[/b], remastered [b]Storming of Dollaran Map[/b] from Dungeons 3, and the [b]Official Dungeons 4 Soundtrack[/b]. Ensuring victory over the heroes of the Overworld. With larger dungeons, an expansive Overworld, enhanced co-op play, more evil critters, and the addition of the infuriating Dwarves, Evil has never looked this good! 

[previewyoutube=BsXN8Om_DMY;full][/previewyoutube]

Building on the success of the iconic Dungeons series, Dungeons 4 unleashes evilness upon the Overworld with a mix of real-time strategy, simulation, and dungeon management gameplay. The story follows the Dark Elf Thalya, recently returned from imprisonment as she sows chaos in in the Overworld and ultimately teams up with a very unlikely partner along with the embodiment of The Absolute Evil re-incarnated, The Baby Evil – Gorgu. Reinforced with a new ability-based Perk System and Baby Evil at her side, Thalya is certain she will finally overcome the forces of good once and for all. 
As if Thalya didn’t have enough to deal with, the developers at Realmforge have decided to make Dungeons 4 even more challenging by adding in a new adversary. [b]Dwarves have arrived in Dungeons 4[/b] ready to tunnel destruction through carefully crafted dungeons to prevent The Absolute Evil from turning the beautiful Overworld into Evil’s most pleasurable holiday paradise. Prepare for the onslaught of Dwarves by ensuring the Dungeon is well-protected by traps and stocked with minions ready to thwart those pesky intruders. Think the Absolute Evil would stop there?  No way! Those brave enough to face the forces of good can have an evil buddy tag along in the adventure with dynamic two-player co-op multiplayer, managing and controlling the same dungeon with a unified evil vision.
What would a new Dungeons game be without the storytelling prowess of the beloved narrator? The undeniably charming and fan-favorite English narrator Kevan Brighting returns to the carnage to chronicle every conquest and provide helpful... or at least satisfying commentary throughout the campaign.

The PC versions on Steam, the Microsoft Store and the Epic Games Store will also include a "beta" version of a level editor that allows users to create and share content.

[b]Dungeons 4 is out now on Steam, with Xbox Game Pass for console and PC Game Pass for PC and is also available on Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation 5[/b]. Dungeons 4 will bring The Absolute Evil to the Nintendo Switch™ in 2024. 

[h2] Features:   [/h2]
[list][*] [b]Everything is better with Dwarves™[/b]: The Dwarves have arrived to build their underground strongholds as the hardy fellows compete with the Ever-Expanding Evil for space and resources.
[*][b] It makes your Dungeon great again[/b]: Dungeons are up to four times larger than before with many more creatures who await the All-Commanding Evil’s orders to conquer the Overworld. Now the time has come for massive armies and truly sprawling dungeons!
[*][b]New and shiny[/b]: An ability-based Perk System for Thalya, the Absolute Evil’s trusted *cough* and most loyal subordinate, grants her impressive new powers. The Absolute Evil can now enjoy taking over the world, governing the creatures and slapping subordinates even more with the customizable Evil Hand.
[*] [b]Minions, everywhere[/b]: The Horde, the Undead, and the Demons wait to do The Absolute Evil’s bidding, with more creatures eagerly following Evil’s orders, and slightly more helpful Snots who will play a much more prominent role this time around.
[*] [b]Many ways to tell the story[/b]: A long campaign, narrated by the beloved English Narrator Kevan Brighting, as well as several skirmish maps all to challenge your rule as the Absolute Evil.
[*] [b]Change the world[/b]: Spread your Evilness across the Overworld to bring lush and green environments over to the dark side, now shining even more vibrant and beautifully evil as you take control over new biomes.
[*] [b]Work together, slay together[/b]: 2-player co-op multiplayer allows both players to manage one Dungeon together with a unified evil vision. All maps from the skirmish mode and the campaign are playable in co-op.[/list]

notes.title: Dungeons 4 FAQ
notes.content:
[h1]Dungeons 4 FAQ[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42842812/a599603207ac36123f6c7bd2d734735cba1a0a71.png[/img]

[b]Genre[/b]	          Strategy / Simulation / Dungeon Management
[b]Release Date[/b]	  November 9th
[b]Age Rating[/b]	  IARC Rating: ESRB Everyone 10+, PEGI 7
[b]Platforms[/b]	  PC, PS5, XBOX SERIES X|S

[h2]What is Dungeons 4?[/h2]
Dungeons 4 is a wholesome Dungeon management game where unicorns mingle among the lush trees; the good side has the high ground and the dark side on Hill Doom has not lived happily after. Oh, come on, which troll has changed the script again? *cough* 
In Dungeons 4, everything is EVIL – again! But everything is now bigger, better, and with even more dynamic Evilness™ – all while keeping the spirit of its predecessor with the return of the Absolute Evil and its trusted *cough* servant, the Dark Elf Thalya. 
You know the drill: gather your evilness, unleash it upon the not-so-evil overworld, secure your fabulously evil Dungeon and bathe in evil laughter while the Overworlders perish. There’s no way some annoying little creatures named dwarves will stand in your way and raid your Dungeon! I mean, what? Get thee gone from my Dungeon, thou gold-grubbing pests!

[h2]What are the main features of Dungeons 4?[/h2]
[list][*] [b]Toss a coin to the Dwarves™:[/b] The Dwarves have arrived to build their underground strongholds and the hardy little fellows (although they don’t like being called that) compete with the Ever-Expanding Evil for space and resources.
[*][b]Harder, better, faster, stronger:[/b] The Gameworld is up to four times larger* than before and there are many more creatures* of the Horde, the Undead and the Demons, eagerly awaiting the Bossy Evil’s orders. Snots will play a much more prominent role this time and are able to level up (less stupidity not guaranteed).
[*] [b]Evilfication is coming to a (new) place near you:[/b] The Overworld is bigger than ever before*. Gain Evilness by beating Mini Bosses or heroes and use it to bring doom to the Overworld, wreaking your Evilfication across many new   biomes. You’re already dead… NANI?!
[*] [b]Let me upgrade you:[/b] An ability-based Perk system for Thalya grants her impressive new powers. The Absolute Evil can now enjoy taking over the world, governing its creatures and slapping subordinates even more with the customizable Evil Hand.
[*] [b]Many ways to tell the story:[/b] A long campaign, narrated by the beloved English Narrator from previous titles, Kevan Brighting, paired with skirmish maps to challenge your rule as the Absolute Evil.
[*][b]Work together, slay together:[/b] 2-player co-op multiplayer* with both players managing one Dungeon together. All skirmish maps and the campaign are playable in co-op.[/list]

[i]*Please note, features marked with * might differ for the Nintendo Switch version. [/i]

[h2]Why should I play Dungeons 4?[/h2]
*The Absolute Evil has entered the chat* You should play Dungeons 4, because…
Everything is bigger! I can now control up to 2x times more creatures, all with new Demon & Horde spells, in an up to 4x times larger dungeon and overworld.* This allows for more creative space with more Dungeon environments (fancy a game of the floor is lava with the heroes?), trap placing with placeable triggers for the traps and more room for evilfication of the overworld across more biomes!
Speaking of heroes, the new dwarf faction is making their way downtown but I – the Trendsetting Evil who can now customize his Evil Hand – care very little about that! Also, my loyal servant and main protagonist of my evil sequel, Thalya, now has a new ability-based perk system, giving her impressive new powers. This allows for another approach to each mission, meaning you can replay the game of evil over and over again. MUHAHAHAHA!
Of course, Dungeons 4 keeps the nicely evil spirit of Dungeons 3, all whilst improving on many systems and mechanics. And – drum roll please – the beloved narrator from Dungeons 3 strikes back for the 20-mission long campaign (Thalya, why the long face?).I If you don’t want to be forever alone in my Dungeon, I’ve also added  2 player co-op multiplayer mode(PvE only)* for individual maps and the entire campaign!

[b]TL;DR – the Dungeons 4 features in a nutshell:[/b]
[list][*] Up to 4x times larger maps and 2x times more creatures (e. g. units, overworld bosses, dungeon creeps)*
[*] A new hero faction: the dwarves
[*] The beloved narrator from Dungeons 3 strikes back – Thalya, why the long face?
[*] More Dungeon environments and biomes – fancy a game of the floor is lava?
[*] Perk system for Thalya, the main protagonist and evil queen of the Dungeon
[*] 2 player co-op multiplayer mode for individual maps and the entire campaign*
[*] Traps with placeable triggers
[*] New spells and potions [/list]
*Please note, features marked with * might differ for the Nintendo Switch version.

[h2]What are the basics of Dungeon Manager in Dungeons 4?[/h2]
The basics of a Dungeon Manager are: Dungeon Managing *ba dum tsss*. In the humorous Dungeons 4, you control your evil creatures in your dungeon and upon the overworld. Managing the creatures’ needs and defending the dungeon from those pesky heroes are your main priority, whilst raiding the overworld and gathering evilness allows for researching new dungeon rooms, creatures, traps, spells and other interesting gadgets. See evil, hear evil, speak evil! 

[h2]What is ‘Evilfication’ in Dungeons 4?[/h2]
If you’re thinking “I don’t know what Evilfication is and, at this point, I’m too afraid to ask” – the Teaching Evil has got you covered! ‘Evilfication’ is an effect that spreads over the Overworld and visually evilfies it by creating evil biomes – with a beautifully evil new look for Dungeons 4! To achieve this Evilfication, you first must gain ‘Evilness’ by defeating an Evil Boss, such as Crystal Golems or those diabolic Unicorns; destroying settlements of the good, villages, strongholds, etc., and now also by defeating heroes! When the heroes resettle or the mini-bosses spawn again, the effect is reversed.

[h2]What kind of evil units does the Absolute Evil control in Dungeons 4?[/h2]
In Dungeons 4, you play as the Evil General Thalya and take control of 3 factions to wreak evilfication across the overworld:
The Horde, the Demons, and the Undead which consist of 4 units each.
The Horde units all have their Champion unit which is unlocked through research. Why settle for a Gnome throwing bombs, when you can have a champion Gnome-piloted, robot monstrosity with UNBELIEVABLE FIREPOWER? After it has been unlocked, the unit will automatically transform into a Champion upon reaching level 7.
The Demons are demonic *bad um tsss – when they are killed, they can be resurrected at a Portal in the Vortex at the cost of Evilness. If no Portal exists, the Demon is lost forever (you wouldn’t want that now, do you?)
The Undead have sold their souls for a full bag of candy (or so they say) and will sleep off their injuries in the graveyard. Additionally, they can all summon their own minions to fight for Evil™.
Can you also convert those pesky, good heroes to join your army of Evil? *Evil nod of approval* Heroes from all 3 factions (Humans, Elves, and Dwarves 🤮) can be stored in the Ice Tomb room in your Dungeon and turned into a Toast, UHM, Ghost Hero (lots of “boos” guaranteed!).

[h2]How does Thalya’s new perk system  work in Dungeons 4?[/h2]
Thalya comes with perks now. In the campaign maps you can find and unlock perks for Thalya, unleashing powerful effects which can give you a big shift in your playthrough experience.
Your greedy creatures ask for gold as salary? One perk allows you to pay them with Gurus instead!
Or, letting the undead minions explode when they ‘die’ sounds like a lot of fun as well…
Choose wisely! Thalya can only have 3 perks at a time, and you can only switch before starting a new map, not whilst playing a map.
This means ultimate replayability and being ultimately evil again, and again, and again – just in different ways!

[h2]What role do the dwarves play in Dungeons 4?[/h2]
Dwarves are your new neighbors who won’t stop banging on the walls with their axes and hammers. The new hero faction competes with you for space and resources in the dungeon by building their own rooms, mining resources and attacking you – dwarves do have a short temper after all *ba dum tsss*

[h2]How does the customization of the Evil Hand work?[/h2]
The Evil Hand is the presence of the Absolute Evil, a visual indicator which interacts with the dungeon environment (and can slap those Little Snots when they don’t work hard enough). In Dungeons 4, you can now customize your Evil Hand by choosing different skins for it that will be then equipped! The Fashionable Evil approves!

[h2]On which platforms will Dungeons 4 be released?[/h2]
Dungeons 4 will be released on Windows PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S consoles and is coming on day one to console, PC, and cloud with Xbox Game Pass, with a version for Nintendo Switch to follow at a later point.

[h2]When will Dungeons 4 be released?[/h2]
Dungeons 4 will be released in 2023 for Windows PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S consoles and is coming on day one to console, PC, and cloud with Xbox Game Pass, with a version for Nintendo Switch to follow later.

[h2]Who is the developer of Dungeons 4?[/h2]
Dungeons 4 is developed by Realmforge Studios in Munich, Germany.

[h2]Will Dungeons 4 include multiplayer?[/h2]
Yes, Dungeons 4 will include multiplayer. The Campaign and skirmish maps are playable in co-op multiplayer with 2 players – PvE only. 
Please note, this feature will not be included in the Nintendo Switch version.
